references.first_campaign: results/v0.7.0-qualification (tooling 82123ae3, freeze 4c03cf7b; evidence v0.7.0-qualification-e75ff6a): NONCONFORMING (campaign), data and verdicts kept unchanged; nothing from it is reused, re-classified or pooled

rules.interval: paired log ratios ln(C/B); n=12 -> one-based order statistics r(3), r(10); n=24 -> r(7), r(18) (analyze_bc_qualification.summarize_metric, unchanged)
rules.classification: PASS if upper <= ln(1+t); REGRESSION if lower > ln(1+t); else INCONCLUSIVE. For higher-is-better metrics the ratio is B/C. IMPROVED is reported (never claimed otherwise) only when the upper bound is below 0.
rules.A: v0.4.0 rules unchanged (analyze_bc_qualification.py --rules v0.4.0), one 12-pair extension per cell with an INCONCLUSIVE gated metric; INCONCLUSIVE_DISCLOSED only for an INCONCLUSIVE primary with median <= t and every supporting metric PASS; else UNRESOLVED
rules.B_C: v0.5.0 protocol sections 3-4 unchanged (tolerances 25/50/100/6%, B5 3.0x, C1-C4); lifecycle scope compact-bfs; window multipliers of run 4 (window-multipliers-dcd8ccc.json) reused unchanged so cells are identical to v0.5.0's; no extension, no rerun
rules.R: 12 analyzed pairs after 2 discarded warmup pairs, fresh process per observation, arm order balanced 6/6 within the analyzed pairs by a seeded shuffle (order seed experiments.R.order_seed); no extension; tolerance primary 10%
rules.Rmem: deterministic allocator byte counts, one run per arm; REGRESSION if candidate > reference x 1.20, otherwise PASS; reported with absolute values
rules.M_desc: descriptive, no verdict; each configuration record classified VALID/INVALID by the validity rule; M5 rule (i) of the v0.6.0 design is re-evaluated descriptively (mean graph-lock wait of the batch job >= 50% of mean client latency for read95/read100 at 16 or 64 closed-loop clients without background activity)
rules.M_reg: 12 analyzed pairs after 2 warmup pairs, a fresh server process per observation, arm order balanced; throughput tolerance primary 10% (ratio B/C), client p99 tolerance query_tail 25%
rules.no_waiver_inheritance: No maintainer waiver or acceptance from v0.6.0 or earlier applies. Every v0.6.0 non-PASS cell (R HTTP import 60/30 REGRESSION, B4 import-high REGRESSION, C3 FAIL x3, A UNRESOLVED x2, INCONCLUSIVE(_DISCLOSED) cells, C4 disclosures) is re-measured under the same rules and reported as measured. This applies equally to the first v0.7.0 campaign: none of its results is accepted, pooled or used to choose cells.
rules.validity: a configuration record is VALID only if errors == 0, item_errors is empty, noop_mutations == 0 and, with background activity, background.failures == 0 and background.completed > 0. 503 refusals are allowed and reported (admission limit 32 pending jobs). For M_reg every analyzed observation must also have only status 200 (unchanged analyzer). An invalid record is reported as invalid, never rerun or dropped; an M_reg cell with any invalid analyzed observation gets no verdict (INVALID).
rules.probe: contention-probe revision 2 (fixes of the v0.6.0 M supplement): KNOTREL_MAX_NODES = nodes + 100000, current ETag for imports, 503 feeder refusals retried after 10 ms and counted, per-item errors and no-op mutations counted, fresh extra-edge IDs per configuration

B_C.question: lifecycle cost and sustained resources on the candidate, same cells and rules as v0.5.0 run 4 and v0.6.0

R.question: lifecycle on: candidate vs published v0.6.0 on import and churn

Rmem.question: lifecycle on: memory peaks candidate vs published v0.6.0

M_desc.question: contention profile of the candidate (probe revision 2)

open_loop.rule: after M-desc, for each of M-standalone-{off,on}-100k config read95-b8-c16: offered rate = f x the closed-loop requests_per_s measured for that config in M-desc, f in {0.5, 0.9, 1.1}; 16 clients, 1 s warmup, 3 s measure, run on a fresh server of the same kind

M_desc.layout: v0.6.0 configurations unchanged; mixed50 configurations run on their own fresh server per kind, and each lifecycle50 configuration on its own fresh server (probe revision 2: lifecycle50 toggles base items and is meant for one configuration per server process)
M_desc.server_processes: 38: the 36 closed-loop servers plus 2 open-loop servers

M_reg.question: contention regression against published v0.6.0 on the v0.6.0 M_reg cells, probe revision 2

host_conditions.power: AC (pmset -g batt first line reports 'AC Power'), checked by the conformance gate before every child of every experiment; failure stops the chain (attempt NONCONFORMING)
host_conditions.thermal: pmset -g therm must report no thermal and no performance warning, checked by the gate before every child of every experiment; failure stops the chain
host_conditions.concurrency: no process outside the allow-list (conformance section) from the start of the quiet period to the end of the chain
host_conditions.activity: allow-list monitor (scripts/conformance_monitor.py) running for the quiet period and the whole chain; per-child gate (scripts/conformance_gate.py) before and after every child of every experiment (A observations, B/C cells, R, Rmem, M_desc and M_reg children)

invalidation.code_change: any change to executed code of knotrel after freezing invalidates every experiment that ran that code; documentation-only commits do not (executed code identity is checked by comparing __TEXT,__text of release builds)
invalidation.tooling_change: any change to a probe, collector or analysis after freezing invalidates the affected experiment
invalidation.failed_child: a failing child stops the experiment; one rerun only for an infrastructure failure unrelated to the measured code, recorded with its cause
invalidation.invalid_runs: kept and reported; never deleted or overwritten (collectors refuse to overwrite)
invalidation.conformance: see conformance.outcome; conformance failures are not infrastructure failures and do not use the one-rerun allowance

resource_ceilings.memory: the host must keep at least 4 GiB free; probes report RSS

budget.basis: durations measured in the first campaign (A 26.7 with 4 extended cells, B/C 7.3, R 1.5, Rmem 0.1, M_desc 11.6, M_reg 13.0) plus about 973 gate checks x ~0.15 s, plus the 120 s grace and 300 s quiet periods; if every A cell needed the extension, about +15

conformance.rule: Nothing outside the allow-list runs, and no user input occurs, from the start of the quiet period to the end of the chain.

classes.order: campaign; zombie -> class of its parent; new controller descendant -> forbidden; PID 0 -> system; deny_basenames -> forbidden; foreground app other than Finder and the Claude desktop app -> forbidden; controller and the chain's ancestors below it -> baseline; Claude desktop app -> baseline; unresolvable live process -> forbidden; Apple-controlled location or system app extension -> system; host_baseline -> baseline; otherwise forbidden
classes.campaign: the chain process and its descendants (PID ancestry)
classes.system: PID 0, or an executable under /System/Library/, /System/Cryptexes/, /System/iOSSupport/System/Library/, /System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/, /usr/libexec/, /usr/sbin/, /sbin/, /usr/bin/, /bin/, /Library/Apple/, or a system app extension /System/Applications/*.app/Contents/PlugIns/*.appex/; never invalidates; CPU time reported
classes.baseline: the controlling Claude Code CLI (validated: a Claude Code CLI executable and an ancestor of the chain) and the chain's ancestors below it; the Claude desktop app (/Applications/Claude.app/); the executables in host_baseline; CPU time reported
classes.forbidden: any other live descendant of the controller at policy time (launch refused) or later (a tool call); any executable on deny_basenames (for an unresolvable process, the comm base name); any registered foreground app (lsappinfo) other than Finder and the Claude desktop app; any unresolvable live process; every process not in the classes above

conformance.host_baseline_note: privileged background helpers that stay resident after their apps quit (inventory of 2026-11-17, scripts/conformance_monitor.py inventory). Any other resident non-system process found at preparation needs a matrix amendment and a new freeze before measuring; it is never allowed silently.
conformance.user_input: HID idle time (ioreg IOHIDSystem HIDIdleTime), read once per second by the monitor and at every gate check, timestamped with the monotonic clock at the read; input is a reading below previous + elapsed - hid_tolerance_s
conformance.liveness: monitor samples the full process table every 0.2 s, writes a heartbeat per sample, and exits if the chain process disappears; gate before every child: monitor PID alive, status age <= 1.0 s, zero violation/HID-reset/HID-failure totals; gate after every child: heartbeats covering the child with no gap > 1.0 s; at chain end: the same over the whole attempt from the quiet-period start
conformance.git_state: read-only snapshot (FETCH_HEAD mtime, remote-tracking reflog sizes) of every clone under /Users/rt/workspace/knotrel before the quiet period and after the chain; any difference is forbidden activity
conformance.cpu_accounting: per child, CPU seconds of system, baseline and forbidden classes from cumulative ps CPU time; disclosure only, no threshold
conformance.outcome: any failed check stops the chain at the next gate and makes the whole attempt NONCONFORMING (no verdict for any experiment of the attempt, completed ones included); data kept; every exit path writes logs/CONFORMANCE.txt, the final Git state and checksums; restart only after the cause is removed, into a new directory, with the same frozen matrix and seeds; at most 3 attempts, then the maintainer decides
conformance.limits: a process that starts and exits between two 0.2 s samples can be missed (CPU accounting and the Git snapshot cover such processes in part); tool calls that start no process are covered only by the transcript check; allowed system processes are not limited in CPU; root-writable firmlinked data directories under /System/Library and /usr/libexec are treated as system; PIDs are not paired with start times (the baseline PIDs are the chain's own ancestors, alive throughout); a SIGTERM to the chain alone takes effect when the current collector ends (the attempt is still NONCONFORMING); rare system dialogs registered as foreground apps (for example Problem Reporter) stop the attempt
conformance.grace_period: between launch and the policy: the operator leaves the Mac and the controller ends its turn; not monitored; at its end the session must be stable for session_stable_s and the HID idle time at least min_hid_idle_at_policy_s, or the launch is refused (NOT STARTED, no attempt consumed)
conformance.controller_transcript: the launch is refused unless the given transcript is under ~/.claude/projects/, was modified in the last 600 s and contains the run_final_chain.sh launch for this campaign; after the grace period, the size and mtime of the transcript and of every file in its session directory (subagent transcripts) must be unchanged for session_stable_s (else the launch is refused); the same state is compared after every step and at chain end, and any change makes the attempt NONCONFORMING
conformance.gating_verification: at chain end, every child each collector recorded must have exactly one conforming gate record (A observations, B/C cells, R/Rmem/M_desc/M_reg children); B/C gates exactly the three declared probe binaries and refuses any other absolute-path program

analysis: A: analyze_bc_qualification.py --rules v0.4.0; B/C: analyze_lifecycle_qualification.py; R/Rmem/M_desc/M_reg: analyze_v070r_qualification.py (the first campaign's analyzers bound to this matrix); conformance: the gate log, CONFORMANCE.txt and analyze_v070_conformance.py-style cross-check of the monitor log
